camera_orbit.observer: sequence of static observers at infinity; no camera-velocity aberration
camera_orbit.screen_basis: continuous rotation in a plane perpendicular to the disk

geometry.model: Schwarzschild null geodesics; first opaque Keplerian thin-disk hit
geometry.delay_definition: coordinate propagation time minus common observer r*; q-r*(hit)
geometry.camera_angle_convention: signed degrees about disk x axis; n=(0,-sin(theta),cos(theta))
geometry.camera_screen_basis: e_x=(1,0,0); e_y=(0,cos(theta),sin(theta)); continuous through both poles
geometry.disk_plane_crossing: positive root psi=pi for noncoplanar rays; coplanar rays first hit outer rim
geometry.disk_surfaces: same prescribed isotropic surface emission on both faces

emission.model: original kinematic source, not NASA software or GRMHD
emission.normalization: exact azimuthal mean equals Page-Thorne at each emission time and radius
emission.loop_assumption: periodically repeated finite-lived source births; not repeating gas orbits
emission.retarded_time: evaluate at t_em=t_obs-delay for each ray

sources.role: orbiting/sheared inhomogeneities as a kinematic model
variable equatorial source, retarded time, orbital scales; not its stochastic solver

layout.safe_area_note: Extra top clearance; interface overlays vary by device and caption state

encoding.rate_control: quality-targeted VBR with a VBV cap; CRF is not a platform requirement
encoding.color_conversion: sRGB RGB to Rec.709 limited-range YCbCr via zscale; pixels transformed before tagging
encoding.conversion_reference: display-referred: sRGB EOTF to linear light, then inverse BT.1886 (gamma 2.4) for Rec.709 display encoding
encoding.instagram_processing: Instagram generates its own delivery encodings; playback quality is not guaranteed by local export

display.color: original illustrative orange brightness palette, not thermal true color
display.averaging: physical bolometric radiance averaged before display transform

scene: original calculation; no NASA images, frames or source code used
time: 800 t_g shown in 8 seconds; periodic source forcing, full 360-degree viewpoint revolution; no physical mass assigned
disk_faces: same isotropic modeled emission field on both faces of a geometrically thin opaque disk

radiance_cache_provenance.note: Reuse of original float radiance; no frames decoded from a previous video
